group noun

of people

also band, set, circle, crowd, in groups, troop, a troop of, bunch (of people), cluster (of people), throng, pack (a theatre), packed

classical

Hor. Ep. 1.9.13: scrībe tuī gregis hunc
Cic. de Or. 1.42: philosophōrum (Lewis & Short)

grex, gregis m.

noun, third declension

a group, a set, a circle of people

Properly a flock; of people, a company or set, in a good or bad sense (Lewis & Short): a circle of friends, a school of philosophers, or a gang (in hunc gregem, Cic. Sull. 77). In groups: gregātim.

Other words

  • caterva, catervae f. — a crowd, a band of people

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Mur. 69: cum bene magnā catervā suā (Lewis & Short)

    In groups: catervātim.

  • circulus, circulī m. — a circle of people talking together

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Cic. Balb. 57: in convīviīs rōdunt, in circulīs vellicant (Lewis & Short)

  • globus, globī m. — a knot, a throng of people

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Liv. 2.29.2 (Lewis & Short)

  • turba, turbae f. — a crowd, throng

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Traupman 299; Traupman 355

  • stīpō, stīpāre, stīpāvī, stīpātum — pack, crowd, throng (a place)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Hor. Ep. 2.1.60: artō stīpāta theātrō, packed into the crowded theatre (Lewis & Short); Traupman 355

Examples

  • scrībe tuī gregis hunc et fortem crēde bonumque

    count him one of your circle, and believe him brave and goodHor. Ep. 1.9.13

  • elephantī gregātim semper ingrediuntur

    elephants always move about in groupsPlin. NH 8.11

See also member, team, class, company, people.
